title: FMB Worldwide | September 18, 2026

entries.headline: Bank of Japan Raises Policy Rate to 1.25%, Highest in 31 Years
entries.verifiedFact: Reuters and AP independently report that the BOJ raised its policy rate from 1.0% to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote, the highest level in 31 years.
entries.whyItMatters: Japan is a major Philippine trade, investment and development partner. Japanese rates can affect the yen, regional capital flows and financing conditions, though direct Philippine household effects are not predetermined.
entries.opportunityRisk: Watch the yen, BOJ guidance, inflation and wage data, and any spillover into Asian financing conditions.

audit.note: ARCHIVE RECOVERY: the BOJ story retained its original September 18 event and publication date. Its source verification and public-domain image rights were rechecked on October 3, and the previously failing canonical public routes were scheduled for fresh post-deployment verification.

deck: Japan’s central bank raised its policy rate to a 31-year high, with regional implications for the yen, capital flows and financing conditions.
